title: Scientific bases for precompetition tapering strategies
journal: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
population: Athletes across sports (review of the taper literature)
findings: Taper defined as a progressive nonlinear reduction of training load during a variable period to reduce physiological and psychological stress of daily training and optimize performance.
Best achieved by maintaining training intensity, reducing training volume (up to 60-90%) and slightly reducing training frequency (no more than 20%).
Optimal duration of the taper ranges between 4 and more than 28 d; progressive nonlinear tapers are more beneficial than step tapers.
Performance usually improves by about 3% (usual range 0.5-6.0%).
limitations: Narrative review by the group that also authored the meta-analysis; ranges are wide (4 to >28 days, volume cut up to 60-90%) and not individualized; population not specified in the abstract.
implications: Frequency floor: never cut run frequency by more than 20% of the pre-taper weekly session count during a taper.

Taper length should scale with preceding load; the 4 to >28 day range is too wide to prescribe from, so the engine caps at 21 days for recreational runners (engine decision, informed by Smyth & Lawlor and Bosquet).
Expected benefit shown to users should be conservative (about 0.5-3%) and phrased as a sketch, not a guarantee.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (MSSE Jul 2003, Mujika first author); abstract text re-read and all findings present. Narrative review so graded D.
